news.title: The women behind UEFA's stand against Infantino's World Cup sell-off
news.lede: UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister and Norwegian Football Federation president Lise Klaveness emerged as two of the leading figures behind European football's opposition to FIFA's abandoned World Cup investment proposal. Citing multiple sources familiar with UEFA's emergency meeting involving around 150 officials, The Athletic reported that McAllister was among the first senior figures to call for a full boycott of FIFA competitions if president Gianni Infantino pressed ahead with plans to sell a minority stake in the commercial rights of the World Cup through the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). The report added that, apart from UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin, no officials were more vocal in calling for decisive action than McAllister and Klaveness.

news.title: UEFA warns FIFA of legal action over failed World Cup sell-off plan
news.lede: European football body UEFA has threatened FIFA with legal action over Gianni Infantino’s failed plan to sell a stake in future World Cup profits to private investors, and said any potential evidence should not be destroyed. Infantino’s secretive proposal to raise US$4.2 billion (NZ$7.1 billion) from investors including the New York investment firm of Joshua Kushner was dropped Saturday, days after the revelation in media reports provoked a global furore. UEFA led the backlash, and on Friday its 55 member federations met to agree to boycott all FIFA events and competitions while the proposal was active. Now lawyers for UEFA have informed FIFA that the European body is “actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints ... arising out of and in connection with the FFE (FIFA Forward Enterprise) plan proposed by FIFA and all related matters”.

news.title: Pochettino to stay as USA coach until 2030 World Cup
news.lede: Mauricio Pochettino has signed a contract extension to remain the head coach of the United States national team until the 2030 World Cup, U.S. football announced on Monday (August 3, 2026). The 54-year-old took over in 2024 and led the USA to the last 16 at the recent World Cup, which they co-hosted with Canada and Mexico. "It has become clear to us that there is tremendous potential to make the men's national team program even stronger," said Argentinian Pochettino, whose coaching staff have also agreed new contracts. "The passion we experienced from the fans throughout the World Cup only strengthened our belief in what is possible here...”

news.title: Gianni Infantino: English FA set to withdraw support for FIFA president as UEFA considers legal action
news.lede: UEFA has threatened legal action against FIFA over Gianni Infantino's World Cup sell-off plan. In a letter addressed to Infantino dated Friday July 31, European football's governing body said it was "actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints" in relation to FIFA's scrapped plan. Key members of the FIFA administration have been warned not to destroy any evidence which may be required during potential litigation proceedings. news.title: FIFA scrap World Cup sell-off plan after backlash
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. FIFA “will not proceed” with plans to sell stakes in a company which would run the commercial and operational aspects of its competitions, a statement from president Gianni Infantino said. The plan, which would include the men’s and women’s World Cups, has been rejected by three continental confederations with UEFA insisting its nations would boycott FIFA events.

news.title: Aleksander Ceferin wants Club World Cup boycott as he plots Gianni Infantino downfall with Nasser Al-Khelaifi talks
news.lede: Al-Khelaifi is one of Ceferin’s key allies and talkSPORT understands the UEFA President is pushing for European Football Clubs (EFC), chaired by Al-Khelaifi, to boycott the 2029 Club World Cup. However, this would require club-wide engagement with the 850+ members. Ceferin has made no secret of his own opposition to the Club World Cup, calling it a 'selfish endeavour' by Infantino back in May 2018. The inaugural 32-team edition was won by Chelsea last summer, but plans for the 2029 event remain completely up in the air.
